<reason>A wins a competitive debate. B identifies a genuine benefit: stopping currently lawful forest and peat conversion. But its comparison relies too heavily on treating tighter rules as uniquely enforceable and household income losses as readily reversible. A undermines both assumptions, distinguishes immediate enforcement from delaying additional restrictions, and exposes B’s inadequate answer on schooling and existing debt. B retains substantial ecological stakes, but A more convincingly challenges whether the proposed additional restrictions justify their additional costs.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A directly refutes B’s claim that burning bans require catching someone mid-fire, then shows that monitoring, permit audits, and buyer scrutiny can support either policy. This substantially weakens B’s claimed enforcement advantage without denying that its prohibitions reach additional land.</best_rebuttal>
